paragraphs: Children in care in Lancashire are looked after by Lancashire County Council's service, Foster for Lancashire, and by the independent agencies listed on this page. The council looks for carers for many kinds of fostering: older children and teenagers, brothers and sisters who need to stay together, children with additional needs, parent and child placements, long-term care, family and friends care, and step-down and pause and reflect placements. In 2022 it launched a campaign aimed specifically at finding homes for children aged 10 and over, saying the need for carers for older children and teenagers was urgent.

To apply you must be over 21 by the end of your assessment, have a spare room for a child's sole use (or plans for one soon), and have lived in the UK for the last six months. You should speak, read and write English fluently or be willing to build those skills. Age, marital status, gender, sexuality, race, religion, disability and employment status are not barriers, and you can own or rent. You do not need to drive, but you must be able to get children to school and to family time. Smokers can foster children over five, but not smoke inside the home.

Every new carer completes the Skills to Foster course, meets regularly with a social worker and can join support groups, and carers' own children have their own groups and activities. The council notes that allowances are paid only while a child is living with you, so it is worth planning for gaps between placements.
If you live in Lancashire, speak to the council and two or three of the agencies below, and compare their training, support and pay before you decide.

sources.title: Foster carers needed in Lancashire for older children and teenagers (Lancashire County Council, 24 November 2022)
